definition_zh: 部分；一份（食物）；应得的份额；命运；（动词）分配
definition_en: a part or share of something larger; an amount of food served to one person; to divide something into shares
core_image: 把一整块切开，把属于你的那一份放到你面前
scene: 每位客人都分到了满满一份烤肉。Each guest received a generous portion of the roast.
sceneCN: 这里 portion 是「分给一个人的一份食物」（第 2 个义项：一份）；句意：每位客人都分到了一份量很足的烤肉。场景要点：整块被切开、按人分、放在各自盘里；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 部分；一份；份额；命运
分配；把……分成份

collocations.zh: 最大的一份（源自狮子分猎物的典故）

derivatives.zh: 没有份额的；无嫁妆的（古）

senses.title: A part of a whole
senses.definition: a part of a larger whole, especially one separated or regarded separately
senses.definitionCN: 一个更大整体中的一部分，尤指被分开或单独看待的那部分
senses.example: A large portion of the budget goes to salaries.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中很大一部分用于工资。
senses.why: Latin portio meant a share assigned to someone. The word begins with the act of cutting a whole and handing out pieces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portio 意为“分派给某人的一份”。这个词起于这样一个动作：把整体切开，再把块分出去。

senses.title: A serving of food
senses.titleCN: 一份（食物）：放到你盘里的量
senses.definition: the amount of food served to one person at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次盛给一个人的食物量
senses.example: Each guest received a generous portion of the roast.
senses.exampleCN: 每位客人都分到了一份量很足的烤肉。
senses.why: Food is the most everyday whole that gets divided. The share on your plate is a portion in the most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 食物是最日常的被分割的整体。你盘里的那一份，就是最具体的 portion。

senses.title: An allotted share of property
senses.titleCN: 应得份额：法律上分给你的那一份
senses.definition: the share of an estate or property that is assigned to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 遗产或财产中分配给某个特定人的份额
senses.example: She received her portion of the family land at twenty-one.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十一岁时得到了属于自己的那份家族土地。
senses.why: Inheritance makes the metaphor legal: the whole is fixed, the shares are named, and each heir gets a portion.
senses.whyCN: 继承把这个比喻法律化了：整体是固定的，份额是有名分的，每个继承人各得一份。

senses.title: One's lot or fate
senses.titleCN: 命运：分给一生的那一份
senses.definition: the share of life, good or bad, that a person is given, in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 文学用语，指一个人被分得的那一份人生，无论好坏
senses.example: He accepted his portion of suffering without complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫无怨言地接受了分给自己的那份苦难。
senses.why: If goods can be allotted, so can experiences. Life itself becomes a whole divided among people, and yours is your portion.
senses.whyCN: 如果财物可以被分派，经历也可以。人生本身成了一个分给众人的整体，你的那一份就是你的 portion。

senses.title: To divide into shares
senses.definition: to divide something into shares and give them out
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干份并发给各人
senses.example: The committee portioned the funds among the three projects.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把资金分给了三个项目。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act that produced it: to portion is to perform the cutting and handing out.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成产生它的那个动作：to portion 就是执行“切开并分发”这件事。

senses.title: To provide with a dowry
senses.titleCN: 给嫁妆：旧时按份给女儿财产
senses.definition: in older usage, to give a daughter a dowry or a share of property at marriage
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指在女儿出嫁时给她嫁妆或一份财产
senses.example: The will portioned his daughters before his sons.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱先给女儿们分好了嫁妆，然后才轮到儿子。
senses.why: A dowry is literally a daughter's portion, the share set aside for her. The verb records that legal practice.
senses.whyCN: 嫁妆字面就是“女儿的那一份”，即为她单留出来的份额。动词记录的就是这一法律习俗。

senses.title: A section of a larger work
senses.titleCN: 章节：一部作品里的一段
senses.definition: one section of a book, document, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 书、文件或乐曲中的一个段落
senses.example: Only a small portion of the report deals with costs.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里只有一小部分谈到成本。
senses.why: A text is a whole too. It can be divided into sections, and each section is a portion of the text.
senses.whyCN: 文本也是一个整体，可以被分成段落，每一段就是文本的一个 portion。

senses.title: An allocated amount
senses.titleCN: 配额：按规定量给你的数
senses.definition: a measured amount of something allocated to a person or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按定量分配给某人或某用途的一份数量
senses.example: The daily portion of grain was weighed out at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 每天那份谷物在黎明时称好分出。
senses.why: When the share is measured rather than simply cut, portion means a fixed quantity: a ration by another name.
senses.whyCN: 当份额是被量出来的而不只是切出来的，portion 就指一个固定数量：换个名字的配给量。

intro.en: Portion comes from a Latin word for an assigned share. The step before it rests on a reconstructed form, so that link is probable rather than directly recorded.
intro.cn: portion 来自拉丁语中表示“分派的份额”的词。它前面的一步建立在重构形式上，因此那一环是“很可能”，而非有直接文献记录。

items.en: Portio meant 'a share, a part, an allotted portion'. It is recorded in classical Latin for shares of property and of food.
items.cn: portio 意为“份额、部分、分得的一份”。古典拉丁语中已用它指财产与食物的份额。

items.en: Portio is generally traced to a reconstructed *partio 'division', related to pars 'part' and ultimately to PIE *pere- (2) 'to grant, allot'. The asterisk marks a form found in no text, so this link is probable rather than documented.
items.cn: portio 一般被追溯到重构形式 *partio“划分”，与 pars“部分”相关，并可再上溯到原始印欧语 *pere- (2)“分配、给予”。星号表示这个形式不见于任何文献，所以这一环是“很可能”，而非有据可查。

items.en: Old French took the Latin accusative portionem and shaped it as porcion, meaning a share or a part.
items.cn: 古法语取拉丁语宾格 portionem，改造为 porcion，意为一份或一部分。

items.en: English borrowed porcion in the early 14th century. Early uses are legal and religious: a share of an estate, a share of goods, an assigned lot in life.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪初借入 porcion。早期用法多属法律与宗教：遗产的一份、财物的一份、被分得的人生际遇。

items.en: The everyday sense 'amount of food for one person' develops later and becomes dominant in modern usage, especially in restaurants and diet advice.
items.cn: “一人份食物量”这一日常义发展较晚，却在现代用法中占据主导，尤其在餐饮与饮食建议里。

items.en: The verb appears alongside the noun, and compounds such as apportion and proportion extend the family. All of them keep the picture of cutting a whole into shares.
items.cn: 动词与名词并行出现，apportion、proportion 等复合词扩展了这个词族。它们都保留了“把整体切成份”的画面。

note.en: The first group is built by adding prefixes to portion itself. The second group collects words for parts and shares.
note.cn: 第一组是在 portion 本身前面加前缀构成。第二组收表示“部分与份额”的词。

entries.definition: to divide and assign in due shares. Ad- 'to' plus portion: to give each their portion.
entries.definitionCN: 按应得的份额划分并分配。ad-“向”加 portion：给每个人应得的那一份。

entries.definition: a relation between parts, or a balanced share. Pro- 'in relation to' plus portion gives the idea of shares measured against each other.
entries.definitionCN: 部分之间的关系，或均衡的份额。pro-“相对”加 portion，给出“份额互相比量”的意思。

entries.definition: changing in a fixed ratio with something else. It extends proportion with -al.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一事物按固定比率变化的。它由 proportion 加 -al 扩展而来。

entries.definition: having no share, especially no dowry. Portion plus -less, common in older legal and literary texts.
entries.definitionCN: 没有份额的，尤指没有嫁妆。portion 加 -less，多见于较早的法律与文学文本。

entries.definition: a piece of a whole. Part is the broad neutral word; portion adds the idea of a share assigned to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一块。part 是宽泛中性的词；portion 多出“分配给某人的份额”之意。

entries.definition: a part belonging to or owed to a person. Share matches portion in legal and financial contexts and is more common there.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某人或应归某人的一部分。share 在法律与财务语境中与 portion 相当，且更常用。

entries.definition: an amount of food for one person. Serving is the everyday restaurant word; portion also carries the sense of an allotted share.
entries.definitionCN: 供一个人吃的食物量。serving 是餐馆日常用语；portion 还带有“分得的份额”之意。

entries.definition: an amount officially given out. Allotment stresses official distribution; portion can be informal or literary.
entries.definitionCN: 官方分发的数量。allotment 强调官方分配；portion 可以是非正式的或文学性的。

entries.definition: a fixed allowance of something scarce. Ration implies shortage and control; portion does not.
entries.definitionCN: 对稀缺物资的固定配给量。ration 含短缺与管制之意；portion 不含。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the slice on the plate, the inheritance, the measured grain, the prefix family, and the fate you are dealt.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：盘里的那一块、遗产里的那一份、量出来的谷物、前缀家族、分给你的一生。

normal.en: Picture a whole roast cut into slices. The slice on your plate is your portion.
normal.cn: 想象一整块烤肉被切成片。你盘里的那一片就是你的 portion。

normal.en: Portion out means hand each person their slice, one by one.
normal.cn: portion out 就是一片一片地把属于各人的那份递过去。

normal.en: In a will, the whole estate is divided and each child gets a portion.
normal.cn: 遗嘱里，整份遗产被切开，每个孩子得到一份 portion。

normal.en: A portion of grain weighed at dawn is a ration under another name.
normal.cn: 黎明时称出的那份谷物，就是换个名字的配给量。

normal.en: Apportion, proportion, portionless: same core, different prefixes and suffixes.
normal.cn: apportion、proportion、portionless：同一个核心，不同的前后缀。

abstract.en: Every whole can be cut, and every cut produces an owner; portion is the word where division becomes possession.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都可被切开，每次切开都产生一个所有者；portion 正是“分割变成占有”的那个词。

abstract.en: A portion is a boundary drawn inside a thing, and boundaries are always drawn by someone.
abstract.cn: 一份是在事物内部画出的一条界线，而界线总是由某个人画的。

abstract.en: When life is called a portion, the metaphor admits that not everything is available to everyone.
abstract.cn: 当人生被称为一份 portion 时，这个比喻承认了：并非所有东西对所有人都是可得的。

examples.en: Only a small portion of the manuscript has survived.
examples.cn: 这份手稿只有一小部分留存下来。

examples.en: Restaurants here are known for generous portions at low prices.
examples.cn: 这里的餐馆以分量足、价格低闻名。

examples.en: The land was portioned among the villagers after the reform.
examples.cn: 改革之后，土地被分给了村民。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖心”——把整颗心剖开，分给每人一份，就是 portion（份额）；注意这只是谐音，与词源无关

root: 拉丁语 portio“份额、部分”（一般追溯到重构形式 *partio“划分”，与 pars“部分”相关，来自 PIE *pere- (2)“分配”）→ 古法语 porcion → 英语 portion（14 世纪初）。

sensesIntro.en: The word always involves cutting a whole and assigning a piece. Food, inheritance, text, and even fate are all wholes of different kinds, and the piece assigned to you is your portion. The verb simply performs that cut.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终涉及“把整体切开并指派一块”。食物、遗产、文本乃至命运，都是不同种类的整体，分给你的那一块就是你的 portion。动词则是执行这一刀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole loaf cut at the table, one slice placed before each person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整条面包在桌上被切开，每个面前放上一片。

chain: A PART CUT FROM A WHOLE

branches.en: PART: a piece of any whole, whether a budget or a book.
branches.cn: 部分：任何整体中的一块，无论是预算还是书。

branches.en: MEASURE: the plate and the scale, food and fixed allowance.
branches.cn: 量：盘子与秤，食物与定量。

branches.en: LAW: inheritance shares and the dowry set aside for a daughter.
branches.cn: 法律：继承份额与为女儿单留的嫁妆。

branches.en: FATE: the share of life dealt to a person.
branches.cn: 命运：分给一个人的那份人生。

branches.en: ACTION: the act of cutting and handing out.
branches.cn: 动作：切开并分发的行为。

intro.en: Portion has generated a small family through prefixes that specify direction or relation (to, for, in ratio) and suffixes that make adjectives and verbs.
intro.cn: portion 通过表示方向或关系的前缀（向、为、按比例）以及构成形容词与动词的后缀，衍生出一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun portio and its related verb forms supplied the base; English built the rest with native endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 portio 及其相关动词形式提供了基底；其余部分由英语用本土词尾构造。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 分配者（苏格兰法律用语）

items.meaningCN: 部分（与 portio 关系未证实）

definition_zh: 位置；方位；姿势；职位；立场；处境；安置；使处于
definition_en: the place where someone or something is, the way the body is arranged, a job, an opinion on an issue, a situation, or to put something in a particular place
core_image: 棋盘上一枚棋子被手指捏起，轻轻放进一个新的格子
scene: 比赛暂停时，教练把几枚棋子从棋盘边角挪到中央，又退后看了看。He moved the knight into a stronger position on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 position 是「位置」（第 1 个义项：某物所在的地方）；句意为他把马挪到棋盘上更有利的位置。图中可辨识物件：棋盘、棋子、教练。

pos.zh: 位置；方位；姿势；职位；立场；处境
安置；使处于（某位置）

derivatives.zh: 由 position 加 -al 构成，义为「位置的；与位置有关的」
由 position 加 -ing 构成，义为「定位；摆放」
由 position 加 -er 构成，义为「定位器；定位装置」

senses.title: The place where something is
senses.definition: the exact place where a person or thing is or should be
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物所在或应在的确切地点
senses.example: The map marks the position of every well in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地图标出了山谷里每一口井的位置。
senses.why: Latin ponere means to place, and positio is a placing; the first sense is the result of that act, the spot where something has been put.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置，positio 是「放置」这一动作；第一个义项就是动作的结果——某物被放定的那个点。

senses.title: The way the body is held
senses.definition: the way someone stands, sits or holds the body
senses.definitionCN: 人站立、坐着或摆放身体的方式
senses.example: Sit in a comfortable position with your back straight.
senses.exampleCN: 挺直背，以一种舒服的姿势坐好。
senses.why: A body placed this way or that forms a visible arrangement, so the placing word comes to name the shape the body makes.
senses.whyCN: 身体这样摆或那样摆，会形成看得见的安排；于是「放置」这个词开始指身体摆出的形状。

senses.title: A job or official role
senses.definition: a job in an organization, or the rank someone holds
senses.definitionCN: 在一个组织中的工作，或某人所居的级别
senses.example: She applied for a position in the research department.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了研究部的一个职位。
senses.why: A post is a place in an ordered structure: the person is placed in it, and the word for the placing becomes the word for the slot.
senses.whyCN: 职位是有序结构中的一个位置：人被放进这个位置，于是表示「放置」的词变成了表示「位置、空缺」的词。

senses.title: An opinion on an issue
senses.definition: the opinion someone takes on a question, especially one they are prepared to defend
senses.definitionCN: 某人对某个问题所持的看法，尤指愿意为之辩护的看法
senses.example: The committee took a firm position against the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会坚决反对修建这条新路。
senses.why: A standpoint is a place one stands; taking a position is choosing where to stand in an argument, so spatial placing turns into opinion.
senses.whyCN: 立场就是站的地方；表明立场就是在争论中选定站处，于是空间上的「放置」变成了看法。

senses.title: To put something in place
senses.definition: to put someone or something in a particular place or arrangement, often carefully
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物放到特定地点或安排中，往往带有仔细的意味
senses.example: He positioned the lamp so that the light fell on the page.
senses.exampleCN: 他把灯安置好，让光落在书页上。
senses.why: The noun names the resulting place; the verb is the act of producing it, and English formed the verb from the noun in modern times.
senses.whyCN: 名词指放置之后形成的位置；动词则是产生这个位置的动作，英语到近代才由名词造出这个动词。

intro.en: Position is the Latin verb ponere, to place, turned into a noun through its participle positus; English took it from French and later made a verb of it again.
intro.cn: position 是拉丁动词 ponere（放置）经其过去分词 positus 变成的名词；英语从法语借入，后来又把名词重新做成动词。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and its past participle positus meant placed or set.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、安放，它的过去分词 positus 意为被放置的。

items.en: Positio was the abstract noun for a placing, and it could already mean the place a thing occupied.
items.cn: positio 是表示「放置」的抽象名词，当时已经可以指某物占据的位置。

items.en: Old French passed position to English in the fourteenth century as a word for a place or an arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把 position 传给英语，指位置或安排方式。

items.en: The word gained the senses of a military post, a job and a stated opinion, all built on the idea of a place one occupies.
items.cn: 这个词陆续获得军事据点、职位与明确看法等义项，全部建立在「所占之处」这一想法上。

items.en: Modern English formed the verb to position and added phrases such as market position, keeping the old placing core.
items.cn: 现代英语造出动词 to position，并添上 market position 一类说法，保留的仍是古老的「放置」核心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb ponere; the near-meaning group gathers words for place, stance and job.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁动词 ponere 构成的词；近义组收表示地点、立场与职位的词。

entries.definition: Relating to position or place.
entries.definitionCN: 由 position 加 -al 构成，义为「位置的；与位置有关的」。

entries.definition: From Latin positivus and positus; it first meant placed or fixed, and now means affirmative.
entries.definitionCN: 与 positus 同根，原指被放置、被定下的，现代义为「肯定的」。

entries.definition: To put together, from com- plus ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-（一起）与 ponere（放置）构成，义为「组成；创作」。

entries.definition: To put down, from de- plus ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de-（向下）与 ponere（放置）构成，义为「存放；沉积」。

entries.definition: The place where something is.
entries.definitionCN: 位置；地点；强调地理上的所在，不指姿势或立场。

entries.definition: A public attitude towards an issue, or the way the body stands.
entries.definitionCN: 立场；站姿；同时覆盖态度与身体姿态。

entries.definition: A job or a place where someone is stationed.
entries.definitionCN: 职位；岗位；强调被派驻的工作地点。

entries.definition: The act of putting something in a place, or a job arranged for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 安置；安排；强调安排的动作或实习岗位。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on the Latin verb for placing, and its family keeps returning to spots, postures, posts and stands.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁语表示「放置」的动词，同族词反复回到地点、姿势、职位与立场。

normal.en: Ponere means to place, and its participle positus is the stem behind position, positive and posit.
normal.cn: ponere 意为放置，它的过去分词 positus 正是 position、positive 与 posit 共同的词干。

normal.en: Compose is com- plus ponere, to put together; deposit is de- plus ponere, to put down.
normal.cn: compose 是 com- 加 ponere，意为放在一起；deposit 是 de- 加 ponere，意为放下。

normal.en: Positional adds -al and simply describes anything about place or arrangement.
normal.cn: positional 加 -al，只用来描述与位置或安排有关的事物。

normal.en: A job is a position because a person is placed into a slot in an organization.
normal.cn: 职位之所以叫 position，是因为人被放进组织中的一个格子里。

normal.en: A position in an argument is a place to stand, which is why one word covers location and opinion.
normal.cn: 争论中的立场就是站的地方，所以一个词同时覆盖位置与看法。

abstract.en: A position is where you are, but also where you choose to stand, and English lets one word hold both.
abstract.cn: 位置既是你所在之处，也是你选择站立之处，英语让一个词同时装下两者。

abstract.en: On a board every piece has a position, and changing it changes what the piece can do.
abstract.cn: 棋盘上每枚棋子都有位置，改变位置就改变了它所能做的事。

abstract.en: To be in position is to be ready, which is why the word appears in sports, jobs and arguments alike.
abstract.cn: 就位就是准备好了，所以这个词在体育、职场与争论里都会出现。

examples.en: He moved the knight into a stronger position on the board.
examples.cn: 他把马挪到棋盘上更有利的位置。

examples.en: She applied for a position in the research department.
examples.cn: 她申请了研究部的一个职位。

examples.en: The committee took a firm position against the new road.
examples.cn: 委员会坚决反对修建这条新路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡贼神」——把棋子摆到棋盘上的某一点，那个点就定了；position 就是位置，也是职位与立场。

root: 源自拉丁 ponere（放置）的过去分词 positus，再由抽象名词 positio 经古法语进入英语；同族词有 compose、deposit、positive。注意与来自 portare（搬运）的 port、portable 区分：position 的核心是「放」，不是「搬」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place something occupies; the senses branch into physical location, body posture, a job slot, a standpoint, and the act of placing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是某物所占据的地方；义项由此分出物理位置、身体姿势、职位空缺、立场，以及放置的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chess piece lifted between two fingers and set down in a new square.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘上一枚棋子被手指捏起，轻轻放进一个新的格子。

branches.en: a marker pinned to a spot on a map
branches.cn: 钉在地图某点上的标记

branches.en: a back held straight in a chair
branches.cn: 椅子上挺直的背

branches.en: a name written into an empty slot on an org chart
branches.cn: 组织架构图空格里写下的名字

branches.en: a delegate standing to state a view
branches.cn: 代表站起来陈述看法

branches.en: a camera positioned to catch the whole stage
branches.cn: 被安放好以拍到整个舞台的相机

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin verb for placing, its participle and an action suffix, and the same pieces also build compose and deposit.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「放置」动词、它的过去分词与一个动作名词后缀构成，同样的部件还造出了 compose 与 deposit。

latinIntro.en: Position comes from Latin ponere, to place, through its participle positus and the noun positio; the same verb also gives compose and deposit.
latinIntro.cn: position 来自拉丁 ponere（放置），经由过去分词 positus 与名词 positio；同一个动词还给出 compose 与 deposit。

items.meaning: forming nouns of action or result
com- plus ponere, to put together
items.meaningCN: 由 com- 与 ponere 构成，意为放在一起

items.meaning: de- plus ponere, to put down
items.meaningCN: 由 de- 与 ponere 构成，意为放下

definition_zh: 积极的；肯定的；正面的；确凿的；阳性的；正的；正电的；原级
definition_en: optimistic or hopeful; expressing agreement or certainty; showing that something is present; (of a number or charge) above zero
core_image: 在一张横轴上，站在零点右边，并明确说「是」
scene: 即使被第三次拒绝，她依然保持积极。She stayed positive even after the third rejection.
sceneCN: 这里 positive 是「心态积极的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：即使被拒三次，她仍然保持积极。场景要点：方向朝上、向前看、不垮；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 积极的；肯定的；确凿的；阳性的；正的
正面之处；正数；（摄影）正片

derivatives.zh: 实证主义（只承认可观察事实）
假定；提出（与 positive 同出 positus）

senses.title: Optimistic and hopeful
senses.titleCN: 积极的：朝好处看的那种劲头
senses.definition: expecting good things and focusing on what can go well
senses.definitionCN: 期待好事、把注意力放在能顺利之处
senses.example: She stayed positive even after the third rejection.
senses.exampleCN: 即使被拒三次，她仍然保持积极。
senses.why: The word's core is 'laid down, definite'. A positive mind is one that has settled on the good outcome rather than leaving it open.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是“被确定下来”。积极的心态，就是把结果定在好处上，而不是让它悬着。

senses.title: Expressing agreement or yes
senses.definition: expressing agreement, approval, or an affirmative answer
senses.definitionCN: 表达同意、赞许或肯定回答
senses.example: We received a positive reply within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 我们一天之内就收到了肯定的答复。
senses.why: A positive answer is one that has been fixed: not maybe, not pending, but settled in the affirmative.
senses.whyCN: 肯定的回答是被固定下来的回答：不是也许，不是待定，而是定在“是”这一边。

senses.title: Good or beneficial in effect
senses.titleCN: 正面的：带来好结果的那一面
senses.definition: producing a good or useful effect
senses.definitionCN: 产生良好或有用的效果
senses.example: The new bus route had a positive impact on local shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新公交线路对本地商铺产生了正面影响。
senses.why: What is settled and real tends to be counted on the good side. Positive becomes the label for effects we want more of.
senses.whyCN: 被确定、被落实的东西往往被算在好的一边。positive 成了“我们希望更多”的效果的标签。

senses.title: Definite and undeniable
senses.titleCN: 确凿的：摆在那里，不容否认
senses.definition: clear, definite, and not open to doubt
senses.definitionCN: 清楚、确定、不容怀疑
senses.example: We have positive proof that the letter was forged.
senses.exampleCN: 我们有确凿证据证明这封信是伪造的。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: in law, positive meant formally laid down. What is laid down is not a matter of opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：在法律上，positive 指正式规定下来的。被规定下来的，就不是意见问题。

senses.title: Medical: showing the condition is present
senses.titleCN: 阳性的：查出了那个东西
senses.definition: showing that a particular substance, infection, or condition is present in a test
senses.definitionCN: 表示在检测中发现某种物质、感染或状况确实存在
senses.example: He tested positive for the virus but had no symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病毒检测呈阳性，但没有症状。
senses.why: A test is a yes-or-no question put to the body. Positive means the thing asked about is definitely there, not absent.
senses.whyCN: 检测是向身体提出的一个是非题。positive 表示所问之物确实存在，而非缺席。

senses.title: Mathematics: above zero
senses.definition: of a number, greater than zero
senses.definitionCN: 指数值大于零
senses.example: Multiplying two negative numbers gives a positive result.
senses.exampleCN: 两个负数相乘得到正数结果。
senses.why: On a number line, positive marks the direction that counts upward from zero. The sign is a settled direction.
senses.whyCN: 在数轴上，正号标记从零点向上计数的方向。这个符号是一个确定下来的方向。

senses.title: Physics: carrying positive charge
senses.titleCN: 正电的：与电子相反的那种电荷
senses.definition: having the kind of electric charge carried by protons, opposite to that of electrons
senses.definitionCN: 带有质子所携的那种电荷，与电子所带电荷相反
senses.example: The positive terminal is marked with a plus sign.
senses.exampleCN: 正极用加号标出。
senses.why: Franklin's convention named one kind of charge positive, and the label stuck. It is a naming decision, not a claim about which charge is better.
senses.whyCN: 富兰克林的约定把其中一种电荷命名为 positive，这个叫法沿用至今。它是命名决定，并不表示哪种电荷“更好”。

senses.title: Grammar: the base degree
senses.definition: in grammar, the simple form of an adjective or adverb, before comparison
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指形容词或副词未作比较的简单形式
senses.example: Good is the positive degree; better and best are the comparative and superlative.
senses.exampleCN: good 是原级；better 与 best 分别是比较级和最高级。
senses.why: The base form states a quality outright, with nothing added. It is the form laid down before any comparison modifies it.
senses.whyCN: 原级直接陈述一种性质，不加任何东西。它是任何比较来改动之前就已定下的形式。

intro.en: Positive comes from a Latin adjective meaning 'settled by agreement'. Its history runs from law to logic to mathematics to electricity, and only recently to optimism.
intro.cn: positive 来自一个意为“经约定确定下来”的拉丁形容词。它的历史从法律走到逻辑、数学、电学，而“乐观”这一义其实很晚才出现。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place'. Its past participle positus, 'placed, set down', is the stem of the whole family: position, deposit, compose, positive.
items.cn: ponere 意为“放置”。其过去分词 positus“被放置的、被定下的”，是整个词族的词干：position、deposit、compose、positive。

items.en: Positivus meant 'settled by agreement, conventional'. In medieval law it described rules laid down by authority, as opposed to natural law.
items.cn: positivus 意为“经约定确定的、约定俗成的”。在中世纪法律中，它指由权威制定下来的规则，与自然法相对。

items.en: English positive appears in the 14th century first in legal and philosophical writing, with the sense 'formally laid down, absolute'.
items.cn: 英语 positive 于 14 世纪出现，最早见于法律与哲学写作，意为“正式规定的、绝对的”。

items.en: By the 15th and 16th centuries it means 'definite, not open to doubt', and it also enters grammar for the uncompared degree of an adjective.
items.cn: 到 15、16 世纪，它表示“确定的、不容怀疑”，并进入语法，指形容词未作比较的原级。

items.en: From the 18th century the word labels the direction above zero and, after Franklin, the kind of electric charge called positive. Photography later adds the positive image.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，这个词标记零点以上的方向；在富兰克林之后，又标记被称为正的那种电荷。摄影随后又加上“正片”。

items.en: The everyday sense 'hopeful, optimistic' is a 20th-century development. It is the newest layer and is not found in the older legal or scientific uses.
items.cn: “充满希望、乐观”的日常义是 20 世纪的产物。它是最新的一层，在较早的法律或科学用法中找不到。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin participle. The second group collects words for approval, certainty, and good effect.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个拉丁分词上。第二组收表示赞同、确定与良好效果的词。

entries.definition: in a positive way, or absolutely. It also serves as an intensifier: positively dangerous means definitely dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 以积极的方式，或绝对地。它也用作强调词：positively dangerous 意为“绝对危险”。

entries.definition: to suggest or assume something as a fact. It comes from Latin positus, the same participle behind positive.
entries.definitionCN: 提出或假定某事为事实。它来自拉丁 positus，即 positive 背后的同一个分词。

entries.definition: a place or a point of view. From positio, a noun built on the same participle positus.
entries.definitionCN: 位置或观点。来自 positio，由同一个分词 positus 构成的名词。

entries.definition: the antiparticle of the electron, with positive charge. Formed in the 1930s from positive plus electron.
entries.definitionCN: 电子的反粒子，带正电。20 世纪 30 年代由 positive 与 electron 拼合而成。

entries.definition: expecting good outcomes. Optimistic is narrower than positive, which also covers agreement, proof, and electric charge.
entries.definitionCN: 期待好结果。optimistic 比 positive 窄，后者还覆盖赞同、证据与电荷。

entries.definition: saying yes or giving support. Affirmative matches sense 02 and is the formal opposite of negative.
entries.definitionCN: 说“是”或给予支持。affirmative 对应第 2 义项，是 negative 的正式反义。

entries.definition: sure about oneself or an outcome. Confident describes the feeling; positive can describe both the feeling and the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己或结果有把握。confident 描述感受；positive 既可指感受，也可指证据。

entries.definition: helpful and intended to improve something. Constructive fits sense 03 and stresses usefulness rather than mood.
entries.definitionCN: 有益且意在改进的。constructive 对应第 3 义项，强调有用性而非情绪。

entries.definition: clear and certain. Definite matches sense 04 and is close to the older core of positive.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而确定的。definite 对应第 4 义项，贴近 positive 较古老的核心义。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the plus side of the axis, the firm yes, the proof on the table, the test result, and the uncompared adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：轴的正侧、干脆的“是”、桌上的证据、化验结果、未作比较的形容词。

normal.en: Positive is the plus side: on a number line it points right, and in mood it points up.
normal.cn: positive 是加号那一边：在数轴上指向右，在心情上指向上。

normal.en: A positive answer is a yes that has been nailed down, not a maybe.
normal.cn: 肯定的答复是被钉死的“是”，不是“也许”。

normal.en: Positive proof is evidence placed on the table where nobody can talk it away.
normal.cn: 确凿证据就是摆到桌上、谁也说不掉的证据。

normal.en: A positive test means the thing you asked about is definitely there, like a light turning on.
normal.cn: 阳性检测意味着你问的那个东西确实在，就像一盏灯亮了。

normal.en: In grammar the positive degree is the plain form before any comparison touches it.
normal.cn: 语法上的原级，就是任何比较来碰它之前的朴素形式。

abstract.en: Positive originally meant settled by authority, not cheerful; the modern smile is a late guest in an old legal house.
abstract.cn: positive 本指“由权威定下”，并非“愉快”；现代的笑脸是这座古老法律宅子里晚来的客人。

abstract.en: A plus sign is a decision about direction, not a discovery about value.
abstract.cn: 加号是关于方向的决定，而不是关于价值的发现。

abstract.en: To call evidence positive is to say the question is closed; that is why the word can sound both reassuring and dangerous.
abstract.cn: 把证据称为 positive，等于宣布问题已经关闭；所以这个词听上去既可让人安心，也可让人警觉。

examples.en: The study found a positive correlation between sleep and test scores.
examples.cn: 这项研究发现睡眠与考试成绩之间存在正相关。

examples.en: Two of the samples tested positive for the bacteria.
examples.cn: 其中两份样本的细菌检测呈阳性。

examples.en: Try to frame the feedback in positive terms before listing the problems.
examples.cn: 在列举问题之前，尽量用正面措辞来组织反馈。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖则提夫”——把好处剖出来、提出来给大家看，就是 positive（积极的、正面的）

root: 拉丁语 ponere“放置”的过去分词 positus → positivus“经约定确定的” → 英语 positive（14 世纪，先用于法律与哲学）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is 'settled, laid down'. A settled answer is affirmative; settled evidence is proof; a settled direction on the axis is plus; a settled charge is positive; a settled outlook is optimism. The grammatical sense is simply the form before comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是“被确定、被定下”。确定下来的回答是肯定；确定下来的证据是确凿；轴上确定下来的方向是正；确定下来的电荷是正电；确定下来的看法是乐观。语法义则只是比较之前的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark placed firmly on the plus side of a line, with nothing left open.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一条线的正侧牢牢按下记号，不留任何悬而未决。

branches.en: CERTAINTY: the firm yes and the proof that closes the question.
branches.cn: 确定：干脆的“是”，以及关闭问题的证据。

branches.en: VALUE: the hopeful outlook and the good effect it expects.
branches.cn: 价值：乐观的心态，以及它所期待的良好效果。

branches.en: DIAGNOSIS: the test that finds the thing present.
branches.cn: 诊断：查出某物确实存在的检测。

branches.en: SIGN: the plus side of the number line and of the electric charge.
branches.cn: 符号：数轴与电荷的正侧。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the plain degree, stated before any comparison.
branches.cn: 语法：任何比较之前的朴素级。

intro.en: Positive is built from a Latin participle plus the adjective ending -ivus. The same stem, with different prefixes, yields most of the place-and-state vocabulary of English.
intro.cn: positive 由一个拉丁分词加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成。同一个词干配上不同前缀，产出了英语里大量表示“放置与状态”的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin positus is the pivot: every word below either contains it or is built by adding a prefix to the verb it comes from.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 positus 是枢纽：下面每个词要么含有它，要么是在其来源动词上加前缀构成。

items.meaning: tending toward, having the nature of
items.meaningCN: 倾向于；具有……性质的形容词后缀
表示状态或性质的名词后缀
表示学说或体系的词尾

latinEntries.meaningCN: 经约定确定的；约定俗成的

definition_zh: 拥有；具备；支配；附身
definition_en: to own something, to have a quality or ability, or to control a person's mind as a spirit does
core_image: 一只手按在椅背上，以主人身份稳稳坐定
scene: 拍卖行的灯已经调暗，木槌悬在半空，围观的人屏住呼吸。The collector possesses a small gold watch that once belonged to a railway engineer.
sceneCN: 这里 possess 是「拥有」（第 1 个义项：作为财产持有某物）；句意为这位收藏者拥有一只曾属于铁路工程师的小金表。画面里有调暗的灯、悬起的木槌和一只旧表。

pos.zh: 拥有；具备；支配；（鬼神）附身

collocations.zh: 你着了什么魔；你怎么会这样

derivatives.zh: possess 加表示「人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「拥有者；持有人」
possess 加 -ive 构成，义为「占有欲强的；所有格的」
self 与 possessed 复合，义为「沉着冷静的」，字面是「自我掌控的」

senses.title: To own something as property
senses.definition: to have something as your own property, especially something valuable or legally held
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为自己的财产持有，尤指贵重或依法持有的东西
senses.example: The family possesses two farms and a small orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人拥有两座农场和一小片果园。
senses.why: The Latin verb possidere pictured a master sitting over a place, so the earliest sense is holding property with authority rather than merely touching it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 possidere 的画面是主人坐在一处地方之上，所以最早的义项是带着支配意味地持有财产，而不只是碰到它。

senses.title: To have a quality or ability
senses.definition: to have a particular quality, skill or feature as part of what you are
senses.definitionCN: 作为自身的一部分而具备某种品质、技能或特征
senses.example: She possesses an unusual memory for faces.
senses.exampleCN: 她对人的面孔有非同寻常的记忆力。
senses.why: Once the word could hold a visible thing, it could hold an invisible one too: a quality is treated as something a person carries around.
senses.whyCN: 词一旦能「持有」看得见的东西，也就能「持有」看不见的东西：品质被看成人随身带着的一样东西。

senses.title: To take hold of someone's mind
senses.definition: of a feeling or idea, to fill someone's mind so strongly that it controls their behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或念头强烈占据某人的心神，以至于左右其行为
senses.example: A wild hope possessed him as he read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 读那封信时，一个狂热的希望攫住了他。
senses.why: The step from owning objects to owning a mind is short: whatever fills your thoughts is felt as having moved in and taken the chair.
senses.whyCN: 从占有物品转到占有一个人的心神，只差一小步：凡是填满你念头的东西，都会被感觉成搬了进来、坐上了主位。

senses.title: To enter and control a person, as a spirit
senses.definition: of a spirit or demon, to enter a person and control what they say and do
senses.definitionCN: 指鬼魂或恶魔进入人体，控制其言行
senses.example: In the story a restless ghost possesses the youngest daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里，一个不安的鬼魂附上了最小的女儿。
senses.why: This is the literal picture behind the third sense: an outside power physically occupying a body, which was later borrowed as a metaphor for strong feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这是第三个义项背后的字面画面：一种外在力量实体般占据了身体，后来才被借去比喻强烈的情绪。

intro.en: Possess comes from a Latin verb that joins the idea of being able with the idea of sitting, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: possess 来自一个把「有能力」与「坐」合在一起的拉丁动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *poti- meant powerful or lord, and it is generally thought to lie behind the Latin words for ability and mastery.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 *poti- 表示「有力量的、主人」，拉丁语中表示能力与主宰的词都从它而来。

items.en: Latin joined potis, able or powerful, with sedere, to sit, making possidere, literally to sit as master over something.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 potis（有能力的、有权的）与 sedere（坐）合起来，构成 possidere，字面就是「以主人身份坐在某物之上」。

items.en: The noun possessio named both the act of holding and the thing held, and its stem possess- carried that meaning into the other forms of the family.
items.cn: 名词 possessio 既指持有的行为，也指被持有的东西，词干 possess- 把这一含义带进这一族的其他词形。

items.en: Old French possesser, recorded from the twelfth century, meant to own or to hold, and it entered English in the centuries after the Norman settlement.
items.cn: 古法语的 possesser 自十二世纪起有记录，意为拥有、持有，在诺曼人定居之后的几个世纪里进入英语。

items.en: Modern English kept the legal and everyday sense of owning, then extended the word to qualities a person has and to a spirit taking over a mind.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了法律与日常两种「拥有」义，再把词义扩展到人所具备的品质，以及鬼神占据一个人的心神。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the same Latin family of holding; the near-meaning group collects plainer verbs for having and keeping.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个表示「持有」的拉丁词族；近义组收更朴素地表示「有、留住」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun of state built on the same Latin stem, meaning the holding or the thing held.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干上的名词，表示持有这一状态或被持有的东西。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who tends to hold on to things or people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容总想把人或物抓在手里的。

entries.definition: The person who holds or owns something.
entries.definitionCN: 持有或拥有某物的人。

entries.definition: To take property or land away from someone by force or law.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力或法律手段剥夺某人的财产或土地。

entries.definition: To have something as your property, the plainest verb for it.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物，是最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To have something in your hands or under your control.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拿在手里，或置于自己控制之下。

entries.definition: The most general verb for something being yours or being with you.
entries.definitionCN: 最笼统的「有」，表示某物属于你或在你身边。

normalIntro.en: The word holds together a Latin adjective of power, a verb of sitting, and two English suffixes that turn it into a person and a tendency.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把表示权力的拉丁形容词、表示坐的动词，以及两个把它变成「人」和「倾向」的英语后缀箍在一起。

normal.en: Potis in Latin meant able or powerful, and sedere meant to sit, so possidere was to sit as master over a thing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 potis 意为有能力的、有权的，sedere 意为坐，所以 possidere 就是坐在某物之上当主人。

normal.en: The double s is real: possess keeps the s of the Latin stem possess-, so it is never written posses or posess.
normal.cn: 双写 s 是真实的：possess 保留了拉丁词干 possess- 的 s，所以绝不写成 posses 或 posess。

normal.en: Possessor swaps the verb ending for -or, the suffix for a person, and names the one who holds.
normal.cn: possessor 把动词词尾换成表示人的 -or，指的就是持有的人。

normal.en: Possessive adds -ive, the suffix of tendency, so it describes a person inclined to hold on.
normal.cn: possessive 加的是表示倾向的 -ive，形容一个人总想抓住不放。

normal.en: Self-possessed uses the same verb in the sense of controlling oneself, and means calm rather than wealthy.
normal.cn: self-possessed 用的是这个词「掌控自己」的一面，意思是从容镇定，而不是富有。

abstract.en: Picture a hand resting flat on a chair arm: owning begins as the confidence to sit down and stay.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平放在扶手椅上：拥有最初就是一种敢坐下来、不走的底气。

abstract.en: A quality you possess is something invisible that you carry the way you carry a key.
abstract.cn: 你具备的品质，是一件看不见却随身带着的东西，像口袋里的一把钥匙。

abstract.en: The jump from owning a house to being owned by a fear shows how quickly holding turns into being held.
abstract.cn: 从拥有一栋房子，到被一种恐惧攫住，说明「抓住」与「被抓住」之间只隔一层。

examples.en: The collector possesses a small gold watch from the last century.
examples.cn: 这位收藏者拥有一只上世纪的小金表。

examples.en: He possesses a patience that surprises his students.
examples.cn: 他的耐心让他的学生感到惊讶。

examples.en: A sudden doubt possessed her at the door.
examples.cn: 站在门口时，一阵突如其来的疑虑攫住了她。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕塞死」——东西太多，柜子快被塞死，因为样样都想拥有；记住 possess 是拥有。

root: 拉丁语 potis（有能力的、有权的）与 sedere（坐）合成 possidere（以主人身份坐定、占有），经古法语 possesser 进入英语；同族词都围绕「持有、掌控」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is holding something with authority; the senses then reach from property to invisible qualities, to a mind taken over, and finally to a spirit in possession of a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是带着支配意味地持有某物；义项由此从财物伸向看不见的品质，再伸向被占据的心神，最后落到鬼神占据身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand resting on the arm of a chair, a master sitting firmly in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在椅子的扶手上，主人稳稳坐定。

branches.en: a deed folded inside a wooden box
branches.cn: 折好放在木盒里的地契

branches.en: a voice that remembers every face
branches.cn: 记得每一张面孔的嗓音

branches.en: a hope that will not leave the room
branches.cn: 赖在房间里不肯走的希望

branches.en: a cold draft passing through a locked door
branches.cn: 穿过锁着的门的一股冷风

branches.en: two farms and a talent, both called someone's own
branches.cn: 两座农场与一种才能，都被说成某人的

intro.en: A Latin adjective of power, a verb of sitting, and English suffixes for a person and a tendency carry the whole word.
intro.cn: 一个表示权力的拉丁形容词、一个表示坐的动词，加上表示人和倾向的英语后缀，撑起了整个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: potis, sedere, possidere and possessio all bear on this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族的拉丁词有明确记录：potis、sedere、possidere 与 possessio 都与这个词有关。

items.meaning: to sit as master, to hold
tending to, having the nature of

definition_zh: 拥有；所有物；属地；控球权
definition_en: the state of owning something, the things owned, territory held, or control of the ball in a game
core_image: 腰上挂着一串钥匙，走一步响一声
scene: 搬家那天箱子一只只打开，主人把每件旧物都擦了又擦。Her possessions filled three rooms of the new flat.
sceneCN: 这里 possession 是「所有物」（第 2 个义项：属于某人的东西）；句意为她的物品装满了新公寓的三个房间。画面里有搬家的纸箱和擦拭旧物的手。

pos.zh: 拥有；所有物；属地；控球权

derivatives.zh: dis-（剥夺）加 possess 构成，义为「剥夺……的财产或土地」
同一词干加 -ive，义为「占有欲强的；所有格的」
同一词干加表示人的 -or，义为「拥有者；持有人」

senses.title: The state of owning something
senses.definition: the state of having something as your own, especially when this is recognized by law
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为自己所有的状态，尤指得到法律承认的持有
senses.example: The house has been in the family's possession for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子由这个家族持有一个世纪了。
senses.why: The Latin noun named the act of holding before it named the object, so the abstract state comes first in English too.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词先指持有的行为，后指被持有的物件，所以英语里抽象的「持有状态」也排在前面。

senses.title: Something that you own
senses.definition: a thing that belongs to you, usually used in the plural for someone's personal belongings
senses.definitionCN: 属于你的东西，通常用复数指某人的个人财物
senses.example: She packed her few possessions into one bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己不多的几件东西装进一个袋子。
senses.why: From the state of holding, the word slides to the things held; the plural then becomes the usual way to list them one by one.
senses.whyCN: 从持有的状态滑向被持有的东西，复数形式随后成了把这些东西一件件清点出来的常用说法。

senses.title: Land or territory held by a country
senses.definition: a country or region controlled by another country, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 受另一国控制的国或地区，常用复数
senses.example: The empire's overseas possessions were costly to defend.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国的海外属地防卫起来代价高昂。
senses.why: Since possidere pictured mastery over a place, the political sense of land held by force or treaty grew straight out of that picture.
senses.whyCN: 既然 possidere 的画面就是对一处地方的主宰，靠武力或条约占有的土地这一政治义便直接从那幅画面里长出来。

senses.title: Control of the ball in a sport
senses.definition: in team sports, the time during which one side has the ball and controls play
senses.definitionCN: 在团队运动中，一方持球并控制比赛节奏的那段时间
senses.example: The home side had possession for most of the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在下半场大部分时间里控制着球。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal idea of holding: the side that holds the ball holds the game, so possession names a temporary kind of control.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了法律上的「持有」观念：持球的一方控制着比赛，于是 possession 用来指一种临时性的掌控。

intro.en: Possession is the noun built on the same Latin verb as possess, and it kept the whole range of that verb: holding, the thing held, and land held.
intro.cn: possession 是与 possess 同一个拉丁动词上的名词，完整保留了那个动词的范围：持有、被持有之物、被占有的土地。

items.en: Latin potis meant able or powerful, and it supplied the first element of the verb possidere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 potis 意为有能力的、有权的，它是动词 possidere 的前半部分。

items.en: Possidere combined potis with sedere, to sit, so that owning was pictured as sitting in command of a place.
items.cn: possidere 把 potis 与 sedere（坐）合成，于是拥有被想象成坐在一处地方发号施令。

items.en: The noun possessio covered the state of holding, the object held and land held, a range English took over almost whole.
items.cn: 名词 possessio 涵盖持有的状态、被持有的物件以及占有的土地，英语几乎整套接收了这一范围。

items.en: Anglo-Norman and Old French possession kept the same breadth, and legal French gave the word a firm place in English law.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼语与古法语的 possession 保留了同样的宽度，法律法语又让它在英国法中站稳了位置。

items.en: Modern English counts possessions in the plural for personal belongings, and uses the singular for territory and for control of the ball.
items.cn: 现代英语用复数 possessions 指个人财物，用单数指属地以及比赛中的控球权。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same holding family in its various forms; the near-meaning group gathers words for what a person owns.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个「持有」词族的不同词形；近义组收表示一个人所拥有之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to own or to hold.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，意为拥有、持有。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person or grammar form that claims ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 形容占有欲强的人，或表示所属关系的语法形式。

entries.definition: To strip someone of property or land.
entries.definitionCN: 剥夺某人的财产或土地。

entries.definition: The one who holds what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 持有这个名词所指之物的人。

entries.definition: Things owned, especially land or buildings, and the right to them.
entries.definitionCN: 所拥有的东西，尤指土地房产及其权利。

entries.definition: The small personal things that someone carries or keeps.
entries.definitionCN: 某人随身携带或保存的个人小物件。

entries.definition: Something valuable that a person or company owns.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或公司拥有的有价值的东西。

normalIntro.en: The noun inherits a Latin verb about sitting as master, and its family spreads from a state of owning to the objects, the land, and even the ball.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词继承了一个「以主人身份坐定」的拉丁动词，词族从持有状态铺到物件、土地，甚至球。

normal.en: Potis meant able and sedere meant to sit, so the noun still carries the picture of a master seated over a place.
normal.cn: potis 意为有能力，sedere 意为坐，所以这个名词里仍坐着一位压住场子的主人。

normal.en: The suffix -ion turns the verb into the name of a state, so possession is the holding and not the holder.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ion 把动词变成状态的名字，所以 possession 是持有本身，而不是持有者。

normal.en: The plural possessions is the everyday word for the things scattered through your bags and rooms.
normal.cn: 复数 possessions 是日常说法，指散落在包里和房间里的那些东西。

normal.en: Dispossess adds dis-, away, and reverses the holding: the things are taken out of your hands.
normal.cn: dispossess 加上表示「离开」的 dis-，把持有反过来：东西被从你手里拿走。

normal.en: Legal English keeps possession for land and goods, which is why the word sounds formal in a courtroom.
normal.cn: 法律英语用 possession 指土地与货物，所以这个词在法庭上听起来很正式。

abstract.en: A ring of keys at the waist: each key is a possession, and the ring itself is possession.
abstract.cn: 腰间一串钥匙：每一把是一个所有物，而整串就是「拥有」本身。

abstract.en: Owning is a relation, not a thing, so one word can name both the state and the objects that fill it.
abstract.cn: 拥有是一种关系而不是一件东西，所以同一个词既能指状态，也能指填满这个状态的那些物件。

abstract.en: When a country calls a distant island a possession, the word quietly turns land and people into property.
abstract.cn: 当一个国家把远方岛屿称作 possession，这个词就悄悄把土地和人变成了财产。

examples.en: The old house came into her possession last spring.
examples.cn: 这栋老房子去年春天归她所有。

examples.en: He lost most of his possessions in the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水让他失去了大部分财物。

examples.en: The team kept possession and waited for an opening.
examples.cn: 球队保持控球，等待机会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕塞身」——家当太多，全塞在身上就走不动；记住 possession 是财物。

root: 与 possess 同源，出自拉丁动词 possidere（占有）的名词形式 possessio，词干 possess- 加 -ion；同族词围绕「持有者、被持有物、剥夺」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the state of holding; from it come the things held, the land a country holds, and the temporary holding of a ball.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是持有这一状态；由此分出被持有的东西、一国所占的土地，以及比赛里对球的临时持有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of keys at the waist that sounds with every step.
core.cn: 核心意象：腰间一串钥匙，每走一步就响一声。

branches.en: a deed that proves who may stay
branches.cn: 证明谁有权住下的地契

branches.en: a bag of worn clothes in a doorway
branches.cn: 门口一袋穿旧的衣服

branches.en: an island drawn in one colour on a map
branches.cn: 地图上被涂成一种颜色的岛

branches.en: ten seconds of passing before a shot
branches.cn: 出手前十秒的传导

branches.en: a watch kept for years and worn every day
branches.cn: 珍藏多年、天天佩戴的表

intro.en: The word is the noun of state from a Latin verb of mastery, and its endings mark a person, a tendency, and a reversal.
intro.cn: 这个词是那个表示主宰的拉丁动词的状态名词，它的词尾分别标出人、倾向和反转。

latinIntro.en: The noun rests on a recorded Latin verb and its noun possessio, with potis and sedere as the two elements inside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个名词依托有记录的拉丁动词及其名词 possessio，内部两个成分是 potis 与 sedere。

definition_zh: 海报；招贴画；张贴者
definition_en: a large printed notice or picture put up in a public place; a person who posts letters or messages
core_image: 车站墙上贴着一张大海报，颜色鲜艳，路过的人都忍不住多看一眼
scene: 车站大厅的墙上新贴了一张电影宣传画。A colorful poster by the ticket office promised that the film would open next week.
sceneCN: 这里 poster 是「海报、招贴画」（第 1 个义项：贴在公共场所的大幅印刷品）；句意为售票处旁一张色彩鲜艳的海报预告电影下周上映。

pos.zh: 海报；招贴画；贴在墙上的大幅印刷品

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「邮政；柱子；（网络）帖子」，也是动词「张贴；邮寄」
由 post 加 -age 构成，义为「邮资」
由 poster 与 board 复合而成，义为「海报纸板」

senses.title: A large printed notice for public display
senses.definition: a large printed sheet of paper with a picture or announcement, put up where many people will see it
senses.definitionCN: 印着图画或告示的大幅印刷品，贴在很多人能看到的地方
senses.example: They put up posters to advertise the school concert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们贴出海报为学校音乐会做宣传。
senses.why: To post is to fix something where the public passes; a poster is simply the large sheet that gets posted.
senses.whyCN: post 作动词是把东西固定在公众来往之处，poster 就是那张被贴上去的大纸。

senses.title: A person who posts
senses.definition: a person who posts letters, notices or messages, now often someone who publishes content online
senses.definitionCN: 张贴信件、告示或发送消息的人，现在常指在网上发布内容的人
senses.example: The forum ranks its most active posters every month.
senses.exampleCN: 论坛每月给最活跃的发帖人排名。
senses.why: Adding -er to post names the doer of the action, so the word follows the person wherever posting happens, from a notice board to a forum.
senses.whyCN: post 加 -er 构成动作执行者，于是这个词跟着「张贴」这个动作走，从布告栏一直走到论坛。

senses.title: A large printed sheet mounted on a wall or board
senses.titleCN: 张贴出来的大幅印刷品
senses.definition: a printed sheet fixed to a wall, board or hoarding so that passers-by will read it
senses.definitionCN: 被固定在墙上、布告板或围挡上的印刷品，好让路过的人看到
senses.example: The wall by the gate was covered with campaign posters.
senses.exampleCN: 大门旁的墙上贴满了竞选海报。
senses.why: Posting means fixing something where the public passes; once the sheet is up, it is not a letter but a poster.
senses.whyCN: post 的动作是把东西固定在公众经过之处；纸一旦贴上墙，它就不是信，而是海报。

senses.title: A star of the silver screen
senses.definition: a famous actor, spoken of through the posters that advertise films
senses.definitionCN: 著名的演员，因印在电影宣传海报上而被这样称呼
senses.example: In her youth she was a poster girl for the whole studio.
senses.exampleCN: 她年轻时是整个制片厂的当家女星。
senses.why: Because faces sold films from hoardings, the picture on the poster came to stand for the star it showed.
senses.whyCN: 既然是海报上的面孔在卖电影，海报上的画像便渐渐代指画中那位明星。

senses.title: To put up notices in a public place
senses.definition: to fix notices or placards in public places so that many people will see them
senses.definitionCN: 把告示或标语牌固定在公共场所，让很多人看到
senses.example: The council posterred the area with warning notices.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会在这一带到处贴了警告告示。
senses.why: The verb takes the noun's place of action: to poster an area is to cover it the way a poster covers a wall.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接借用了名词的场所动作：poster 一个区域，就是像海报贴满墙那样把它贴满。

senses.title: The placard carried in a demonstration
senses.definition: a large card with a slogan, carried so that others will read the message
senses.definitionCN: 写有口号、被人举着让别人读到的大卡片
senses.example: Protesters raised posters demanding cleaner air.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议者举起了要求更清洁空气的标语牌。
senses.why: A sign you hold is still a thing posted toward the public, so marches borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 举着的牌子依然是朝公众张贴之物，游行于是借用了同一个词。

senses.title: An animal kept for posting its image
senses.definition: an animal, especially a horse, whose picture is put up to advertise it or its owner
senses.definitionCN: 其画像被印成招贴做宣传的动物，尤指马
senses.example: The stallion was a poster horse at every county fair.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹种马在每次县集会上都是招贴上的名马。
senses.why: Once posters advertise everything, the thing pictured can be named by the paper it appears on.
senses.whyCN: 既然海报能为一切做宣传，被印上的东西也可以用它出现的那张纸来称呼。

senses.title: Something striking enough to be printed big
senses.definition: something whose image or claim is so striking that it seems made for a large printed notice
senses.definitionCN: 形象或宣言醒目到像是专为大幅印刷品而生的东西
senses.example: The ruined tower became a poster image for the whole earthquake.
senses.exampleCN: 那座倒塌的塔成了整场地震的标志性画面。
senses.why: The big, bold sheet is the word's core picture, so anything vivid and public can be called poster-like.
senses.whyCN: 大幅醒目的纸是这个词的核心画面，因此任何鲜明而公开的东西都能带上 poster 的色彩。

intro.en: Poster is built on post, an English word with two Latin sources: the postal sense runs from ponere, the upright-stake sense from popularis, and the poster we hang came through the mailing sense.
intro.cn: poster 建立在 post 之上；post 有两个拉丁来源：邮政义来自 ponere（放置），立柱义来自 popularis，而海报义走的是邮寄这一路。

items.en: Latin ponere meant to place, to put; from it came pausare, to halt, and the idea of setting something down.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置、安放，由此派生出 pausare（停驻），以及「把某物安放下来」的观念。

items.en: Medieval Latin postare gave post, first the fixed stations where mail was set down and changed horses, then the mail itself.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 postare 给出 post，先指放置邮件、换马的固定驿站，后指邮件本身。

items.en: Old French poste carried both the fixed station and the mail that moved between stations; it also named an upright stake, a separate Latin line from popularis.
items.cn: 古法语 poste 兼指固定驿站和往来其间的邮件；它还指立柱，那来自另一条拉丁语线索 popularis。

items.en: English post covered the mail, an upright stake, and the act of fixing a notice where the public passes.
items.cn: 英语的 post 兼指邮件、立柱，以及把告示固定在公众经过之处的动作。

items.en: From post came poster, first the person who posts, then the large printed sheet meant to be posted on walls; today it also names online content images.
items.cn: 由 post 派生出 poster，先指张贴者，后指专供张贴的大幅印刷品；如今也指网上的图片内容。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the post family and one word that only echoes the ending; the near-meaning group gathers printed things meant for the public eye.
note.cn: 形近组收 post 词族的词，另收一个只是词尾相像的词；近义组收面向公众的各类印刷品。

entries.definition: The mail, an upright stake, or the act of fixing a notice; the first element of poster.
entries.definitionCN: 邮件、立柱，或张贴告示的动作；poster 的基础词。

entries.definition: The charge for sending mail, built on post with the suffix -age.
entries.definitionCN: 邮寄费用；由 post 加后缀 -age 构成。

entries.definition: The act of posting a letter or publishing an online message.
entries.definitionCN: 投寄信件或发布网络消息的行为。

entries.definition: A list of names and duties; it echoes the -ster ending but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 值班名单；词尾与 poster 相像，来源不同。

entries.definition: A written or printed announcement put up for people to read.
entries.definitionCN: 张贴出来供人阅读的书面告示。

entries.definition: A printed notice or advertisement, especially one posted in public.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷的告示或广告，尤指贴在公共场所的。

entries.definition: A displayed board or notice giving information or directions.
entries.definitionCN: 提供信息或指引的展示牌、标牌。

normalIntro.en: Everything in the word points back to post: the sheet is made to be posted, and the person is the one who posts it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的一切都回指 post：那张纸是为张贴而做的，那个人是执行张贴的人。

normal.en: Poster = post + er: first the doer, then the thing that gets done to, a sheet for posting.
normal.cn: poster = post + er：先指做动作的人，后指承受动作的东西，即供张贴的大纸。

normal.en: Post ultimately traces to Latin ponere, to place: a poster is simply a picture placed on public view.
normal.cn: post 最终可溯至拉丁语 ponere（放置）：海报就是被放到公众视野里的一幅画。

normal.en: To post a letter and to post a notice use the same word; a poster is the notice enlarged.
normal.cn: 寄信和张贴告示用的是同一个动词；海报就是放大了的告示。

normal.en: The plural is regular: poster becomes posters.
normal.cn: 复数规则变化：poster 变 posters。

normal.en: Online posters are the modern heirs: same word, new wall, the screen.
normal.cn: 网络发帖人是它的现代后裔：同一个词，换了一堵新墙——屏幕。

abstract.en: A poster is a wall speaking: it shouts one picture and five words to everyone passing.
abstract.cn: 海报是一面会说话的墙：向每个路过的人喊出一幅图和五个词。

abstract.en: Posters sell dreams at the height of the eye, exactly where you look while waiting.
abstract.cn: 海报在视线的高度出售梦想，恰好是你等候时会看的地方。

abstract.en: A city without posters is a room with nothing on its walls.
abstract.cn: 没有海报的城市，像一堵什么都不挂的墙围成的房间。

examples.en: They put up posters to advertise the school concert.
examples.cn: 他们贴出海报为学校音乐会做宣传。

examples.en: A colorful poster by the ticket office promised that the film would open next week.
examples.cn: 售票处旁一张色彩鲜艳的海报预告电影下周上映。

examples.en: He designed a poster for the sports meet and posted it near the gate.
examples.cn: 他为运动会设计了一张海报，贴在大门附近。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖斯特」——把海报「剖」开来「贴」上墙，路人都「特」别爱看，这就是 poster。

root: poster 由 post 加执行者后缀 -er 构成；post 经中世纪拉丁语 postare 与古法语 poste 进入英语，邮政义可溯至拉丁语 ponere（放置），立柱义另有来源 popularis，两条线索在古法语交汇。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sheet fixed where the public passes; the senses run from the printed notice itself to the person who posts letters or messages.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是固定在公众必经之处的一张大纸；义项从印好的招贴本身，走到投寄信件、发布消息的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright sheet pasted on a station wall, read by everyone who waits.
core.cn: 核心意象：车站墙上一张鲜亮的纸，等车的人都看它。

branches.en: a film poster by the ticket office
branches.cn: 售票处的电影海报

branches.en: concert posters pasted across campus
branches.cn: 贴满校园的音乐会海报

branches.en: the worker posting bills on the hoarding
branches.cn: 往围板上贴告示的工人

branches.en: an active poster in an online forum
branches.cn: 论坛里活跃的发帖人

branches.en: posters calling for volunteers, posted and reposted
branches.cn: 招募志愿者的海报，贴了又贴

intro.en: The word is a plain English derivation, but its base post carries two Latin lines that met in Old French.
intro.cn: 这个词是简单的英语派生词，但它的基础词 post 带着两条在古法语交汇的拉丁线索。

latinIntro.en: The postal line runs through Medieval Latin postare from ponere; that chain is recorded and listed as the Latin entries.
latinIntro.cn: 邮政一条线经中世纪拉丁语 postare 上溯 ponere；这条链条有据可查，列为拉丁条目。

a person who does the action

latinEntries.meaning: to place at stations, to halt

definition_zh: 研究生；已取得第一学位后继续深造者；研究生阶段的
definition_en: a student who continues study after a first degree, working for a master's or doctoral qualification
core_image: 学位台阶的第二段：同一名学生越过第一级平台，手里的选课单换成了实验记录本
scene: 图书馆顶层的研究间里，几名学生把本科毕业证收进抽屉，桌上摊开的是实验记录与论文草稿，窗外天色已经暗下来。The postgraduate spent two years collecting samples in the coastal marsh.
sceneCN: 这里指「已取得第一学位、继续攻读更高学位的学生」（第 1 个义项：本科毕业之后仍在读研究生课程或做研究的人）；句意为这名研究生花了两年在沿海沼泽采集样本。图中可辨识物件：收进抽屉的证书、实验记录本、论文草稿、采样瓶。

pos.zh: 研究生；攻读硕士或博士学位者
研究生阶段的；研究生课程的

senses.title: A student working beyond the first degree
senses.titleCN: 攻读更高学位的研究生
senses.definition: a student who has already taken a first degree and is now working for a master's or doctoral degree
senses.definitionCN: 已取得第一学位、正在攻读硕士或博士学位的学生
senses.example: The postgraduate spent two years collecting samples in the coastal marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 这名研究生花了两年在沿海沼泽采集样本。
senses.why: post- 'after' plus graduate 'degree holder' names a learner who has stepped past the first degree.
senses.whyCN: 表示「之后」的前缀加「学位持有者」，指已经越过第一学位的学习者。

senses.title: The advanced-study level
senses.definition: the level of study that follows a first degree and leads to a higher qualification
senses.definitionCN: 紧随第一学位之后、通向更高资格的教学层次
senses.example: She joined a postgraduate program in public health.
senses.exampleCN: 她加入了公共卫生方向的研究生项目。
senses.why: before a noun the compound names the level itself rather than the person on it.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前时，这个合成词指层次本身，而不指处于该层次的人。

senses.title: A course or diploma after the first degree
senses.titleCN: 研究生课程或文凭（英式名词用法）
senses.definition: a taught course or diploma taken after a first degree, spoken of as a thing one signs up for
senses.definitionCN: 第一学位之后修读的授课型课程或文凭，被当作可以报名的一件事
senses.example: He signed up for a one-year postgraduate in data science.
senses.exampleCN: 他报读了一个为期一年的数据科学研究生课程。
senses.why: British noun usage can name the course by the level word alone, so the compound stands for the programme itself.
senses.whyCN: 英式名词用法可以直接用层级词指课程，于是这个合成词就代表项目本身。

senses.title: The years of advanced study
senses.definition: the period during which a person studies beyond the first degree
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在第一学位之后继续读书的那段时间
senses.example: Her postgraduate years were split between three laboratories.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究生岁月分散在三个实验室里。
senses.why: as with undergraduate, the name of the person is transferred to the time the person occupies.
senses.whyCN: 与「本科生」同理，指人的词被转用来指人所占的那段时间。

senses.title: The postgraduate body
senses.definition: the whole group of advanced-degree students at an institution
senses.definitionCN: 一所院校里攻读高级学位的学生的整体
senses.example: Postgraduate numbers doubled within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 研究生人数在十年内翻了一倍。
senses.why: institutional usage counts the group as one figure, so the label shifts from a person to the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 院校统计把整组当成一个数字，因此称谓从个人转到全体。

senses.title: A part-time or working postgraduate
senses.definition: a student who combines advanced study with paid employment, often on an evening or modular track
senses.definitionCN: 把深造与工作结合、多走晚间或模块化课程的学生
senses.example: The evening track serves postgraduates who keep full-time jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间课程服务那些保留全职工作的研究生。
senses.why: institutional usage adds the working arrangement to the basic label without changing its degree meaning.
senses.whyCN: 院校用法在基本称谓上补出工作安排，并未改变其学位含义。

senses.title: A registered advanced-degree candidate
senses.titleCN: 注册在册的研究生身份（统计口径）
senses.definition: a person formally registered in an advanced-degree program, as counted by a registry
senses.definitionCN: 正式注册在高级学位项目、被登记口径统计的人
senses.example: The registry counts each postgraduate once, whatever the funding source.
senses.exampleCN: 登记口径对每名研究生只计一次，不论经费来源。
senses.why: registry language needs a single countable person, so the label narrows to whoever is formally enrolled.
senses.whyCN: 登记用语需要可计数的个人，因此称谓收窄为正式在册者。

senses.title: Someone who keeps digging deeper
senses.titleCN: 比喻：已有根基仍继续深入的人
senses.definition: a person who continues to study a subject long after the first stage is done
senses.definitionCN: 在第一阶段完成之后仍长期钻研某一主题的人
senses.example: A postgraduate of city history, she still walks the old streets every week.
senses.exampleCN: 作为城市史的深入研习者，她每周仍去走那些老街。
senses.why: the academic image is extended: the second stair becomes any deeper level of a subject.
senses.whyCN: 学术意象被延伸：第二级台阶变成任何主题的更深层次。

intro.en: Postgraduate joins Latin post 'after' to graduate, itself from Latin gradus 'step, degree'. The compound is a nineteenth-century academic formation.
intro.cn: postgraduate 把拉丁 post「之后」加在 graduate 上，后者出自拉丁 gradus「台阶、等级」；这一合成词是十九世纪学术用语的产物。

items.en: Post meant 'after, behind' in place and in time, and English still uses it as a prefix in dozens of words.
items.cn: 拉丁 post 表示位置或时间上的「之后、在后面」，英语至今用它构成大量词。

items.en: Gradus 'step, degree, rank' gave the academic verb graduare 'to confer a degree'.
items.cn: gradus「台阶、等级、位阶」派生出了表示「授予学位」的学术动词。

items.en: Graduate entered English in the sixteenth century and settled into two uses, the degree holder and the act of taking a degree.
items.cn: graduate 在十六世纪进入英语，稳定为两种用法：学位持有者与取得学位这一动作。

items.en: In the nineteenth century universities needed a word for study that came after the first degree, and the two Latin pieces were joined.
items.cn: 十九世纪高校需要一个词指第一学位之后的学习，于是把两个拉丁部件合在一起。

items.en: British and American spelling agree here, and everyday campus speech shortened the long word to postgrad.
items.cn: 英美拼写在此一致，校园口语又把长词缩成更短的说法。

items.en: Dating note: the mid-nineteenth-century first record is approximate, and the earliest written use cannot be pinned to a single year.
items.cn: 年代说明：十九世纪中叶的最早记录只是约数，最早书证无法锁定在某一年。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the degree stem and are easily mixed up; group two holds other names for advanced students.
note.cn: 第一组是共用「学位」词干、容易混淆的词；第二组是其他指高级阶段学生的说法。

entries.definition: The spoken shortening of postgraduate; it names the same student in fewer syllables.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生一词的口语缩略，用更少的音节指同一类学生。

entries.definition: A person who already holds a degree; the prefix is what turns this into a learner who continues.
entries.definitionCN: 已经持有学位的人；正是那个前缀把它变成继续深造的学习者。

entries.definition: From Latin postumus 'last', later respelled as if it contained post 'after'; it has nothing to do with study.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语中表示「最后的」一词，后来被误按「之后」的前缀改写；与学业毫无关系。

entries.definition: Built with the same prefix but attached to doctoral, so it marks the stage after a PhD rather than after a first degree.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀相同但接在「博士的」一词上，标的是博士之后而非第一学位之后。

entries.definition: The usual American term for the same person; British usage prefers the single compound.
entries.definitionCN: 美式常用说法，指同一类人；英式更常用单个合成词。

entries.definition: A student who has passed the qualifying stage of a doctorate; narrower than postgraduate.
entries.definitionCN: 已通过博士资格阶段的学生，范围比研究生窄。

entries.definition: A student working for a master's degree only; postgraduate also covers doctoral work.
entries.definitionCN: 只攻读硕士学位的学生；研究生的范围还包括博士阶段。

entries.definition: A person employed to investigate; the label describes the job rather than the registration status.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇从事研究的人；这个词描述工作而非注册身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real prefixes, real relatives and real campus phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实前缀、真实同族词与真实校园说法。

normal.en: post 'after' + graduate 'degree holder': the learner who comes after the first degree.
normal.cn: 表示「之后」的前缀加「学位持有者」：第一学位之后的学习者。

normal.en: The pair undergraduate and postgraduate face each other across the same degree line.
normal.cn: 「本科生」与「研究生」隔着同一条学位线相对而立。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: postgraduate study, postgraduate research, postgraduate supervisor.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：研究生学习、研究生科研、研究生导师。

normal.en: The prefix also builds postdoctoral, the stage after the doctorate.
normal.cn: 同一前缀还构成「博士后的」，即博士之后的阶段。

normal.en: Campus speech clips it to postgrad.
normal.cn: 校园口语把它缩略成更短的形式。

abstract.en: Picture a hiker who has passed the first lookout and is now climbing toward the summit.
abstract.cn: 想象一名徒步者走过第一个观景台，正朝山顶继续爬。

abstract.en: Picture a second volume of a series, thinner but denser than the first.
abstract.cn: 想象一套书的第二卷，比第一卷薄，却更密实。

abstract.en: Picture a tree adding a new ring after the trunk is already formed.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树在主干成形之后又长出一圈新年轮。

examples.en: The postgraduate spent two years collecting samples in the coastal marsh.
examples.cn: 这名研究生花了两年在沿海沼泽采集样本。

examples.en: Postgraduate study in this department requires a statistics course.
examples.cn: 本系的研究生学习要求修一门统计学课程。

examples.en: She supervised six postgraduates and two visiting researchers.
examples.cn: 她指导了六名研究生和两名访问研究者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「之后」加「毕业者」：毕业之后再接着读的人，就是研究生

root: 拉丁 post「之后」加 graduate「学位持有者」，后者源自拉丁 gradus「台阶、等级」；gradus 更早的来源一般认为是「行走、迈步」类词根，具体形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses run from the advanced student, through the level and the course, to the years, the group, the part-time case, the registry label and finally to any deeper digger.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「高级阶段的学生」出发，经过层次与课程，走到岁月、群体、兼读情形、登记身份，最后落到任何继续深挖的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second flight of stairs above the first landing, with a notebook instead of a timetable in the climber's hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一平台之上还有第二段台阶，攀登者手里的课程表换成了记录本。

branches.en: PERSON AND REGISTRY: the individual learner and the same learner as counted by a registry.
branches.cn: 人与登记：单个学习者，以及同一学习者在登记口径里的身份。

branches.en: LEVEL AND COURSE: the advanced stage and the taught program taken as a product.
branches.cn: 层次与课程：高级阶段，以及被当作一项产品的授课项目。

branches.en: YEARS AND GROUP: the span one person fills, then everyone filling it together.
branches.cn: 岁月与群体：一个人占满的时间，再是所有人共同占满的时间。

branches.en: PART-TIME CASE: the same label carried by someone who also works.
branches.cn: 兼读情形：同一称谓落在同时工作的人身上。

branches.en: BORROWED DEPTH: the second stair becomes any deeper level of a subject.
branches.cn: 借用的深度：第二段台阶变成任何主题的更深层次。

intro.en: Postgraduate is a Latin prefix on an English word of Latin origin, and the pieces also build the names of neighbouring academic stages.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁前缀加在一个拉丁来源的英语词上，同样的部件还构成相邻学术阶段的名称。

latinIntro.en: Latin post supplies the prefix; gradus supplies graduate graduation gradual; doctoral adds the highest stage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 post 提供前缀；gradus 提供 graduate、graduation、gradual；doctoral 则补出最高阶段。

items.example: The prefix marks the stage that follows the first degree.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出第一学位之后的阶段。

items.example: A graduate has finished the first climb.
items.exampleCN: 学位持有者已经完成第一段攀登。

items.example: The ending turns the degree noun into a verb of conferring.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把学位名词变成表示授予的动词。

items.meaning: a learner after the first degree
items.meaningCN: 第一学位之后的学习者

items.example: Postgrad is what students say in the corridor.
items.exampleCN: 学生在走廊里说的就是那个缩略形式。

items.example: Postdoctoral work follows the highest degree.
items.exampleCN: 博士后工作接在最高学位之后。
她的博士后阶段持续了三年。

items.meaning: the act or ceremony of conferring degrees
items.meaningCN: 授予学位的动作或典礼
items.example: Graduation is the gate the postgraduate has already passed.
items.exampleCN: 毕业典礼是研究生早已走过的那道门。

definition_zh: 推迟；延期；暂缓；把……置于次要地位；使延缓发生
definition_en: to move an event or decision to a later time, to keep something from happening yet, or to place one thing after another in order or importance
core_image: 行李箱上的日期签被撕下，重新贴上一张更晚的日子
scene: 赛前一夜下起大雨，球场边的排水沟满得往外溢，裁判举着喇叭跟两队教练商量。The referee decided to postpone the match until the following weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 postpone 指「把比赛改到更晚的时间」（第 1 个义项：活动延期举行）；句意为裁判决定把比赛推迟到下个周末。图中可辨识场景：积水的球场、举着喇叭的裁判、围在边线旁的两队教练。

pos.zh: 推迟；延期；暂缓；使居次位

senses.title: To move an event to a later time
senses.definition: to arrange for an event, appointment or journey to take place later than was planned
senses.definitionCN: 把活动、约会或行程安排在比原计划更晚的时间
senses.example: They postponed the wedding until the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把婚礼推迟到春天举行。
senses.why: The Latin verb postponere is built from post, after, and ponere, to place, so the event is literally put further back on the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 postponere 由 post（在后）与 ponere（放置）组成，事情就是被「放到日历更靠后的位置」上，所以是改期。

senses.title: To leave a decision or action for later
senses.definition: to delay dealing with a decision or action without abandoning it
senses.definitionCN: 暂不处理某个决定或行动，但并没有放弃它
senses.example: The committee postponed its verdict on the disputed plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会暂缓就那份有争议的方案作出裁决。
senses.why: Ponere only says where a thing is put, so the verb can put a decision aside just as easily as it puts a date back, and either way the matter stays open.
senses.whyCN: ponere 只交代「把东西放在哪儿」，所以这个动词能把决定搁到一边，也能把日期往后挪，两种做法都让事情悬着。

senses.title: To place something after another in rank
senses.definition: to treat one thing as less urgent or less important than another and let it come second
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事的紧迫性或重要性低于另一事，让它排在后面
senses.example: He postponed his own career so that his brother could study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他把自己事业的事往后放，好让弟弟出国读书。
senses.why: The spatial picture turns abstract: priority is also a line with things placed along it, and whatever is put behind has to wait its turn.
senses.whyCN: 这个空间画面转向抽象：优先次序同样是一条排队线，被放到后面的东西就得等轮到自己。

senses.title: To slow a process so that it happens later
senses.definition: to hold back a natural or gradual process so that its results appear at a later stage
senses.definitionCN: 使自然的或渐进的过程放慢，让结果出现得更晚
senses.example: Early treatment can postpone the worst effects of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 早期治疗可以延缓这种疾病最严重的影响。
senses.why: If a single event can be placed later on a calendar, a process with an expected end can be pushed back in the same way, and that is how the verb reaches illness and ageing.
senses.whyCN: 既然一件事能在日程上往后放，一个有预期终点的过程也能照样往后推，动词于是走进了疾病与衰老这类话题。

intro.en: Postpone is Latin postponere carried into English almost whole: post meant after and ponere meant to place, so the word has always been about putting something further back.
intro.cn: postpone 几乎原样搬自拉丁语 postponere：post 意为「在后」，ponere 意为「放置」，所以这个词从头到尾说的都是把东西往后放。

items.en: Ponere meant to put, set or place, and it built a large family of English words about position and arrangement.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、安放，它造出了一大批表示位置与排列的英语词。

items.en: The prefix post meant after or behind, whether the distance was measured in space or in time.
items.cn: 前缀 post 意为「在后」，既可量空间，也可量时间。

items.en: Postponere joined the two: to put one thing after another, and in later usage to put an affair off to a later date.
items.cn: postponere 把两者合起来：把一物放到另一物之后，后来也指把事情挪到更晚的日子。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century, first for placing things in order, then for shifting dates and plans.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，先用于按次序摆放，随后用于改动日期与计划。

items.en: Modern English uses it mainly for dates, decisions and processes, while the older ranking sense survives in formal writing.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用它谈日期、决定与过程，较早的「排序」义则留在正式书面语里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin verb ponere; the near-meaning group collects verbs for moving something to a later time.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁动词 ponere 构成的词；近义组收表示把事情挪到更晚时间的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of placing, and every sense is a different place on a line: a calendar, a queue of priorities, a process running late.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语里表示「放置」的动词，每个义项都是同一条线上的不同位置：日历、优先次序的队列、走慢了的过程。

normal.en: Post- means after and ponere means place, so postpone is simply to place after.
normal.cn: post- 意为「在后」，ponere 意为「放置」，postpone 就是「放到后面」。

normal.en: The family shares ponere: component is put together, opponent is put against you, position is where a thing is put.
normal.cn: 这一族词共用 ponere：component 是被拼在一起，opponent 是被放到你对面，position 是被放置的地方。

normal.en: A postponed match has a new date; a postponed decision has no date at all, only a later one.
normal.cn: postponed 的比赛有新日期；被搁置的决定根本没有日期，只有「以后」。

normal.en: The noun is postponement, and it takes -ment like movement and agreement.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 postponement，和 movement、agreement 一样加 -ment。

normal.en: Formal writing still says that one aim is postponed to another, meaning placed below it.
normal.cn: 正式书面语里还会说某个目标被 postponed to 另一个目标，意思是排在它之下。

abstract.en: To postpone is to move a thing down a line without taking it off the line.
abstract.cn: 推迟是把一样东西在队伍里往后挪，而不是把它从队伍里拿掉。

abstract.en: A calendar is a row of places, and the word treats time as something you can rearrange.
abstract.cn: 日历是一排位置，这个词把时间当成可以重新摆放的东西。

abstract.en: What is put behind still exists; that is why postponement is not cancellation.
abstract.cn: 被放到后面的东西依然存在，所以延期并不等于取消。

examples.en: They postponed the wedding until the spring.
examples.cn: 他们把婚礼推迟到春天举行。

examples.en: The judge postponed the hearing for two weeks.
examples.cn: 法官把听证会推迟了两周。

examples.en: Nothing was cancelled; every item on the list was simply postponed.
examples.cn: 什么都没取消，清单上每一项只是被往后推了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕事拖」——越怕事情办不成，越往后拖；postpone 就是推迟、延期。

root: 拉丁语 post-（在后）+ ponere（放置）→ postponere（放到后面）→ 英语 postpone；同族有 component、opponent、position。

sensesIntro.en: One image of placing runs through the senses: a date moved back, a decision left pending, a task pushed down the queue, a process slowed.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项贯穿着同一个「放置」的画面：日期后移、决定悬着、任务排到后面、过程放慢。

definition_en: possible but not yet actual; having the capacity to develop into something; (noun) the capacity to become something in the future
core_image: 一枚还没拉开的弓：力已经存着，只是尚未射出
scene: 药房里，药剂师指着说明书上的警示行。She said: Potential side effects make this drug dangerous when it is taken with alcohol.
sceneCN: 这里 potential 是「潜在的、可能发生但还没发生的」（第 1 个义项：以一种可能性的方式存在）；句意：潜在的副作用会让这种药与酒精同服时变得危险。场景要点：还没发生、但条件一凑就会发生；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 潜在的；可能的；有潜力的
潜力；可能性；电势；势能
